title: CPU Image Captioning: Application Monitoring
description: DA3408 A4: Streamlit + BLIP (CPU) instrumented with prometheus_client, node_exporter for the host, Prometheus + Alertmanager for alerting.

panels.title: How to read this dashboard

options.content: **CPU-only BLIP image captioning (Streamlit), monitored with Prometheus + node_exporter.** Read top-down: **1 Health** (is it alive?) → **2 Throughput & latency** (how much work, how fast?) → **3 Workload** (what kind of work?) → **4 System resources** (what does it cost the machine?). Colours are colourblind-safe (Okabe-Ito) and fixed per entity: ■ single mode / machine user CPU · ■ bulk mode / caption-app process · ■ machine system CPU. Dashed lines = the second series in a panel and **circle markers = single mode**, so series stay distinguishable in grey-scale print. Shaded regions = a bulk ZIP job was running (annotation). Every chart: title = *topic: what it shows* · named axes with units and scale (all **linear**) · a legend whenever there is more than one series · hover ⓘ for the story (query, normal values, what to look for).

panels.title: 1 · Health: is the app alive and ready to caption?
App reachable
panels.description: Prometheus' own `up` metric for the python_app scrape target. UP = the /metrics endpoint on :18000 answered the last scrape (1s ago). DOWN = the Streamlit process is not running or not reachable. Fires the CaptionAppDown alert after 5s.

panels.title: Model ready
panels.description: Gauge caption_model_loaded set by the app: READY once BLIP has loaded. The metrics server starts before the model, so the app can be UP but NOT READY during start-up; this panel separates the two.

panels.title: Firing alerts
panels.description: Number of Prometheus alerts currently FIRING (any rule in rules.yml). 0 is healthy. Details on :9090/alerts and :9093 (Alertmanager).

panels.title: Requests in progress
panels.description: Gauge caption_active_requests summed over modes: requests being processed right now. Normally 0; 1 while a caption or bulk job runs.

panels.title: Errors (last 15 min)
panels.description: increase() of the caption_errors_total counter over 15 minutes, all stages (model_load, decode, zip, inference). Skipped files inside ZIPs are NOT errors; they are counted separately in row 3.

panels.title: Time since last caption
panels.description: Seconds since the last successful caption (time() minus gauge caption_last_success_timestamp_seconds). Grows steadily when idle; resets to ~0 each time an image is captioned.

panels.title: 2 · Throughput & latency: how much work, how fast?
Throughput: images captioned per second, by mode
panels.description: Recording rule caption:images_processed:rate1m = per-second rate of the counter caption_images_processed_total{status="success"} over a 1-minute window, split by mode. A bulk ZIP job shows as a plateau of ~0.5-0.6 images/s (≈1.7 s per image on this CPU); single uploads show as small bumps.

panels.title: Latency: inference time per image, p50 and p95
panels.description: Recording rules caption:inference_seconds:p50_1m / p95_1m = histogram_quantile() over the caption_inference_seconds histogram (1-minute window), by mode. p95 = 95% of images were captioned faster than this. Dashed reference lines: 4 s warning and 8 s critical thresholds of the HighInferenceLatency alert. Normal: p50 ≈ 1.7 s, p95 ≈ 2 s. Colour = percentile (p50 blue, p95 green); line style = mode (bulk solid, single dashed with markers).

panels.title: Latency distribution: how many images fell in each inference-time bucket
panels.description: Heatmap of the caption_inference_seconds histogram buckets: sum by (le) (increase(..._bucket[30s])). Each column is a 30 s slice, each row a latency bucket (upper bound, seconds); darker = more images. A healthy CPU keeps the dark cells in the 1.5-2 s rows; overload pushes them upwards.

panels.title: Requests per minute, by client and mode
panels.description: increase() of the counter caption_requests_total over 1 minute, split by the custom labels client_ip and mode. One request = one single-image caption OR one whole bulk ZIP job. Shows WHO is using the app (client metadata labels).

panels.title: Average inference time by beam width (num_beams)
panels.description: Mean seconds per image for each beam-search width chosen with the sidebar slider: rate(caption_inference_seconds_sum[5m]) / rate(caption_inference_seconds_count[5m]), grouped by the beams label. beams=1 is greedy decoding; each extra beam keeps one more candidate caption alive, so CPU time per image grows with the beam width.

panels.title: 3 · Workload: what kind of work is the app doing?
Bulk job progress
panels.description: Gauge caption_bulk_progress_ratio: fraction of the current bulk ZIP job done (0-100%). Stays at 100% after a job finishes until the next one starts.

panels.title: Caption length: number of captions per word-count bucket (all time)
panels.description: Bucket counts of the caption_length_words histogram (all modes). Each bar = captions with at most that many words. Typical BLIP captions are 7-11 words; captions in the +Inf bar would be runaway repetitive outputs (this is how a 'gi gi gi…' bug was found and then verified fixed).

panels.title: Runtime info: what is running and what it costs to start and feed
panels.description: Context for reading the other panels. Device/model: Info metric caption_build_info (labels device, model, torch_version), proof that inference runs CPU-only. Model load time: gauge caption_model_load_seconds = cold-start cost after a restart (explains a brief NOT READY on 'Model ready'). Avg ZIP extraction: histogram caption_zip_extract_seconds, _sum / _count since start; tiny compared with inference, so bulk time is model time. Avg input image size: histogram caption_image_megapixels, _sum / _count; BLIP resizes every image to 384×384, so input size does not drive latency.

panels.title: Files skipped inside ZIPs: count by reason (all time)
panels.description: Counter caption_files_skipped_total by reason label. Bulk mode never crashes on bad input: non-images, corrupt/truncated images, macOS system files, oversize files and files over the 50-image limit are skipped and counted here.

panels.title: Upload volume: bytes received per second, by mode
panels.description: rate() of caption_upload_bytes_sum (a Summary: _sum = total bytes, _count = number of uploads) over 1 minute, by mode. A ZIP upload is a short spike of ~1 MB.

panels.title: Average end-to-end request time, by mode
panels.description: Summary caption_request_seconds: rate(_sum[5m]) / rate(_count[5m]) = average seconds per request over 5 minutes. Single ≈ 2 s; a bulk request covers the whole ZIP (e.g. 27 images ≈ 46 s).

panels.title: 4 · System resources: what does captioning cost the machine?
CPU cores busy: whole machine vs caption-app process
panels.description: Machine (node_exporter): recording rule cpu_util = sum by (mode) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode=~"user|system"}[30s])), i.e. CPU-seconds per second = cores in use. App (prometheus_client): rate(process_cpu_seconds_total{job="python_app"}[30s]). During a bulk job the app line rises to ~6-8 cores and the machine 'user' line follows it: the app is the cause of the spike. Dashed line at 2 cores = CPUMoreThan200Percent alert.

panels.title: Memory: machine RAM used vs caption-app resident memory
panels.description: Machine: node_memory_MemTotal_bytes − node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes. App: process_resident_memory_bytes{job="python_app"} (≈2 GB with BLIP loaded). The app's share stays flat during bulk jobs: images are processed one at a time.

panels.title: Disk I/O: bytes read and written per second (all disks)
panels.description: rate() of node_disk_read_bytes_total and node_disk_written_bytes_total over 30 s, summed over disks. Captioning is CPU-bound, so disk stays quiet; a spike at app start = model loading from cache.
